operations.summary: Queue an owned server OS update plan, OS update or reboot
operations.description: Requires the Edge-signed `techstack.servers.maintenance` entitlement, ownership of the server in the tenant, and current server-bound standing authority for delegated native MCP calls. These three ordinary actions require no fresh MFA or separate owner_approved assertion. Reboot and os_update require expected_impact_digest from the preview the user confirmed. Impact is compared atomically at admission and again at execution claim; changed or incomplete evidence sends no command and requires a refreshed preview and renewed confirmation with a new request key. The body is decoded strictly: exact lowercase keys, no duplicates, no unknown fields. A replay with the same Idempotency-Key returns the stored receipt before target validation. One reboot or OS update and, separately, one update plan may be active per server; a job not finished by its deadline fails with `deadline_exceeded` and frees its slot. The action is offered in `allowed_actions` only when the server agent advertises `stackkit.host-maintenance.v1`, and `reboot` only when the server also reports `host_boot_id`. Refusals are client-error-envelope/v1 documents; 409 `reason_code` is one of control_plane_host, substrate_node, protected_demo_server, service_locked, maintenance_active, node_operation_active, plan_stale, agent_capability_missing, boot_id_unknown, agent_not_connected, heartbeat_stale, inventory_revision_stale, idempotency_key_reused, impact_confirmation_required, impact_changed or impact_unavailable; 403 carries entitlement_required or maintenance_origin_authority_denied.

operations.summary: Repair named drifted host security controls
operations.description: Requests a bounded repair of controls the fresh host security evidence reports as drifted and automatically repairable. Requires the server's owner, the Edge-signed `techstack.servers.maintenance` entitlement and a fresh multi-factor sign-in (at most 300 seconds old). The repair travels as a typed, journaled Guard command that runs `stackkit host security repair --apply` for exactly the named controls; StackKits refuses, before changing anything, a change that would cut the management path or lock the owner out. Bounds: one repair per server at a time (409 `repair_in_progress`), a per-control cooldown (429 `repair_cooldown`), a daily attempt budget per control (429 `repair_attempts_exhausted`) and a circuit breaker after consecutive failures (429 `repair_circuit_open`); the 429 answers carry `retry_after`. A control that is compliant (409 `control_not_drifted`), under an approved exception (`control_has_exception`), manual (`control_not_repairable`), blocked on an authorized SSH key (`needs_authorized_key`) or not observed is refused. The body is decoded strictly.

Creates or resumes one deterministic Add-Server job for the exact
owned StackKit deployment. The standard `Idempotency-Key` is mandatory.
Replaying the same key with the same canonical request returns the original
job, lease, runtime-server, resource-generation, and provider-operation

The raw key is never persisted or returned. A lost response or an
uncertain native-admission outcome remains resumable only with the

provider reconciliation is pending; it never claims that the VM is
already provisioned or healthy. Fresh admission atomically reserves
the authenticated tenant/owner capacity slot with the lease generation
and provider operation. When authoritative native admission finds that
bounded capacity full, it persists a non-retryable 403 outcome and
replaying that denied job returns the same outcome. Exact replays of an
already committed admission reuse its existing reservation. This version
has no automatic reservation release: terminal or local decommission
state alone does not free a slot. Lease inventory and feature-delivery
flags never authorize or deny capacity.
Hosted fresh admission also requires the v2-signed commercial runtime
and provider entitlements plus the signed `cloud.runtime.credits`
`managed_servers` mode/limit decision; feature flags alone never grant
provider capacity. Self-host OSS uses its construction-fixed static
release-manifest policy instead of a SaaS entitlement dependency.

operations.summary: Queue an owned node's typed Advanced or backup operation
operations.description: Uses the same tenant- and owner-scoped dispatcher as the operator UI. The node executes through its authenticated channel, current release pin, native Advanced catalog and issued operation capability. Techstack never executes Terramate, apply, rollback, backup or restore itself. A mutation requires owner_approved; service locks and active server maintenance are checked before enqueue. Direct backup_run and backup_configure remain Basement-only; managed kits keep their schedule and sealed target-renewal authority. backup_configure derives the node's target and plan from existing custody and accepts no credential fields. advanced_change_set requires candidate_spec; rollback requires an exact rollback_target_ref; restore_drill may reuse a snapshot_anchor_id. ai_provider lets Private AI offer an external OpenAI-compatible provider: the kombify Wallet seals the item wallet_item_id (the provider's API key) to the node, which must be listed as a host target of that item, the node binds it to ai_provider_base_url, and a drift reconcile applies the setting. ai_provider_disable removes it. ssh_trust_recipient and ssh_trust_apply let the server trust the owner's kombify Wallet SSH CA: ssh_trust_recipient has the node answer the owner's recipient_challenge with its owner-signed recipient statement and returns it with the host target the owner lists on the CA item; the owner then asks the Wallet for the ssh-ca-trust delivery and ssh_trust_apply hands its sealed_delivery to the node, which installs TrustedUserCAKeys and the principals of each local user. Restore activation requires exactly one Idempotency-Key header, while other operations have no replay guarantee. Acceptance is not execution success; read the returned job and its scoped result to observe effects.

operations.summary: Report kombify Guard host security and backup observations
operations.description: The Guard's posture channel. A full report carries what the Guard observed through the privileged executor's read-only StackKits operations: the `stackkit.host-security-evidence/v1` document of `stackkit host security verify` and the receipt states of `stackkit backup status`. A check-in (`check_in: true`) carries nothing and only asks whether a fresh observation was requested. The identity is the authenticated worker's; the control plane recomputes the verdict from the controls, judges time by its own clock, and records a document it cannot read (unknown schema version, unknown control or state, bad freshness window) as `evidence_rejected`, which leaves no earlier pass standing. A StackKits release without the command is reported as `unsupported` and shows as `security.state: unknown` with `reason_code: stackkit_cli_unsupported`. The answer is the directive: `verify_requested` and the routine cadence, and while the owner's approval of automatic repair is active, `local_policy`: the signed grant of that policy version. Editions without posture answer `state: disabled`. The same channel carries the evidence of a repair the Guard ran on its own under a local policy while the control plane was unreachable (a body with `operation_id`, `GuardLocalOperationEvidence`). It is accepted only against the registered policy version it names (same tenant, worker and exact expiry, a credential generation no newer than the authenticating one, started inside that version's lifetime, for controls it covers, within the persisted cooldown, attempt budget and circuit breaker) and acknowledged only after it is recorded in the server's repair journal. An identical repeat is acknowledged again (`duplicate: true`); anything else is refused with a structured `reason` and leaves no record.

evidence.description: The stackkit.host-security-evidence/v1 document (schemas/stackkit-host-security-evidence-v1.schema.json), at most 256 KiB.

verify_request_id.description: The `verify_request_id` of the directive being answered. Set only on a report whose observation the Guard started after it received that directive; a routine observation carries none.

oneOf.description: Evidence of one repair a Guard ran on its own under a local policy version. The operation ID is Guard-generated and names the policy version (`local:<policy_id>:v<version>:<nonce>`). Each revision is immutable; `report.digest` covers every other field. A first revision is `terminal` or `outcome_unknown`; a later revision only resolves an `outcome_unknown` and names the digest it supersedes.

outcome.description: The stackkit.host-security-repair/v1 outcome of a terminal report.

local_policy.description: The control plane's Ed25519-signed grant of the owner's current repair approval for this Guard (contract `guard.local-repair/v1`, signed with the worker's binding key the Guard pinned at pairing). Absent while no approval is active: the Guard then only observes. The Guard holds it in memory only and drops it on an answer without one. It admits a repair on its own only while the control plane is unreachable, for at most 15 minutes after `issued_at` (the command authority lifetime) and never past `policy_expires_at`, on a clock that agreed with `issued_at` at receipt and still continues from it; after a restart it only observes until a fresh online answer. The privileged executor verifies the signature, the operation ID and the lifetime again before it runs the typed StackKits host-security repair, at most once per operation.

A batch carries records of one source epoch with increasing sequence numbers: each record is one collection cycle of the data contract (host CPU, memory, swap, load, disk per mount, uptime and container resource usage; SERVER-CONNECTION-STANDARD section 9) or an explicit gap marker. The control plane repeats the contract filter, stamps tenant, worker and server from the authentication, stores the samples and acknowledges only what it stored (`acked_sequence`), so a Guard that lost an acknowledgement replays without duplicates and keeps everything else. operations.summary: Confirm the handoff of a retired server's command evidence
operations.description: The owner, as custodian of a detached or retired server, confirms that the command evidence its Guard still holds (journal entries, outcomes and identity state) may leave the server by `export` (an archive the operator takes off the server) or `quarantine` (a root-only directory outside the Guard state). The response shows a one-time `confirmation` exactly once and is valid for 72 hours. It is bound to the host key the worker used. The operator passes it to `techstack agent handoff --server --confirmation-file`, which has the control plane verify it for this server's key, then moves and securely removes the evidence and records a receipt. Pairing a server whose host key served another tenant, or that declares another tenant's evidence, is refused (409 `tenant_handoff_required`) until a receipt of that tenant is consumed. A receipt is consumed once, by the pairing that proves the confirmed key, before expiry; only that pairing may repeat it within 15 minutes (409 `tenant_handoff_invalid` otherwise). Requires the owner and a fresh multi-factor sign-in (at most 300 seconds old). 409 `tenant_handoff_worker_active` while the worker is not revoked or rejected, 409 `tenant_handoff_unbindable` for a worker that never bound a host key. A worker of another tenant or owner is 404.
